source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad
finding: First LLM benchmark that tries to map all three CLT loads: intrinsic difficulty d, distractor ratio (extraneous), and task length N as a proxy for germane load. Length N was the dominant stressor.
numbers: 22 reasoning LLMs; N in {20,50,100,250}; 100 puzzles per config for 13 open models (14,000 per model), 10 per config for Gemini-2.5, gpt-5, DeepSeek-R1. Steepest drop N=20 to 50: DS-Llama-70B 0.89 to 0.66; Qwen3-8B 0.71 to 0.40; gpt-5 1.00 to 0.98; o3 0.99 to 0.98.
quote: task length (N) serves as an operational proxy for conditions demanding germane load
limits: Germane load is NOT measured. Length is only an 'operational proxy'; this is the authors' mapping, not a validated germane-load manipulation. Max context 32K.
agent_relevance: Do not treat long chains as free. Sustained state tracking over many updates is where weaker models break; keep reasoning chains short or checkpoint them (state summaries).

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad
finding: Intrinsic difficulty d hurts most models monotonically, but frontier reasoners barely move.
numbers: d=1 to 3: o3 0.96 to 0.93; gpt-5 1.00 to 0.97; smaller or distilled models drop 0.10-0.25. By d=5, 12 of 22 models are below 50%. At d=10 gpt-5 0.82, o3 0.80, weakest 0.10-0.15.
limits: Synthetic logic puzzles only.
agent_relevance: Element interactivity (how many entities interact) is a usable difficulty knob for sizing sub-tasks for our agent.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad
finding: Distractor ratio gives a U-shaped accuracy curve, not the monotone drop plain extraneous-load theory predicts.
numbers: Most models do worst at intermediate needle-to-hay ratios; U-shape gets deeper as d rises. Regression with a quadratic term fits; NT50 (min relevant fraction for 50% accuracy) is missing for frontier models (always above 50%) and for weak models (never above).
limits: Mechanism unexplained by the authors. Contradicts a simple 'more distractors, worse' reading of CLT.
agent_relevance: Mixed relevant-irrelevant context may be worse than mostly-irrelevant context. Filter context hard or not at all; do not half-filter.

source: Kaiser et al. (2025) CogniLoad
finding: Fitted capacity indices per model: ECL50 (max statements at 50% accuracy), NT50, ID50. Models fall into high, mid and low capacity tiers.
numbers: Low tier (DS-Qwen-7B, Phi-4-mini-reasoning, DS-Qwen-1.5B, Qwen3-1.7B) fail to reach 50% even at mean load.
limits: Frontier models are on only 10 puzzles per config, so tier edges are noisy.
agent_relevance: A cheap load-tier probe could set how much a given model may hold per step in our scaffold.

source: Shang et al. (2026, TMLR) United Minds or Isolated Agents? CoThinker under Cognitive Load Theory
finding: Multi-agent scaffold built from CLT: split intrinsic load across agents, shared memory to cut extraneous load, moderated routing. Helps on high-intrinsic-load tasks, hurts on low-load instruction following.
numbers: Tested on LiveBench with 3 Gemini models plus CommonGen-Hard; paired Holm tests; 16 of 25 comparisons significant per the text. Cross-model: Qwen3-8B, Mistral-7B, GPT-5-Nano, GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen3-30B-A3B.
quote: design-time evidence for the analogy rather than proof of a CLT mechanism inside the model
limits: The CLT mapping is an analogy; authors say proxies are design-time evidence for the analogy, not proof. No germane-load term is modelled.
agent_relevance: Use decomposition and multi-agent only when the task is high element-interactivity. For simple tasks route to one agent.

source: Shang et al. (2026, TMLR) United Minds or Isolated Agents? CoThinker under Cognitive Load Theory
finding: Pilot proxies: attention entropy rises with task difficulty; instruction help lowers perplexity on hard tasks but not on easy tasks (redundancy effect analogue).
numbers: Attention entropy 4.44 / 4.80 / 5.04 for difficulty levels 1-3 (AMPS arithmetic). Hard-task PPL 120.50 -> 88.97 -> 85.35 as instructions get richer (levels 1-3); easy-task PPL 3.37 -> 3.42 -> 3.45.
limits: Perplexity of the answer is a weak proxy for load. Appendix: PPL rises again at instruction levels 4-5 (named strategies, full multi-framework instructions), so there is an inverted-U in instruction size.
agent_relevance: Matches our guardrail idea: more scaffold text helps only up to a point and only on hard items. Scale the schema prompt to item difficulty.

source: Shang et al. (2026, TMLR) United Minds or Isolated Agents? CoThinker under Cognitive Load Theory
finding: Ablation shows the shared-memory (TMS) component is not universally helpful; it hurt on GPT-family backbones that refuse to show reasoning.
numbers: Math subset accuracy, TMS on/styles on vs TMS off/styles on: Qwen3-30B-A3B 81.87 vs 76.41; GPT5-Nano 55.97 vs 62.36; GPT-OSS-20B 57.15 vs 58.37. Styles off (TMS on): 69.79 / 49.02 / 48.21.
limits: Authors attribute GPT drop to refusals like 'I can't provide step-by-step reasoning'. Not tested further.
agent_relevance: Schema-building memory (germane-like) fails if the backbone will not expose intermediate steps; design to synthesise from final answers.

source: Shang et al. (2026, TMLR) United Minds or Isolated Agents? CoThinker under Cognitive Load Theory
finding: Peer-input perplexity for weaker models falls with compression, a CLT load-reduction proxy.
numbers: Qwen3-8B PPL 6.56 baseline, 3.58 with styles, 1.69 with TMS, 3.10 with N=3 references; Mistral-7B 6.63, 5.04, 1.58, 2.86. Reference set size N=2-3 optimal; more agents is non-monotonic.
limits: PPL measured on stronger models' answers, not downstream accuracy.
agent_relevance: Summaries of peer or prior reasoning are easier to absorb than raw transcripts; compress notes between states.

source: Wang et al. (2026, AAAI) Beyond Accuracy: Cognitive Load Framework for Tool-use Agents (ToolLoad-Bench)
finding: Splits tool-use task difficulty into intrinsic load (Tool Interaction Graph) and extraneous load (query ambiguity, distractor tools); accuracy shows cliffs as load rises. No germane term.
numbers: Overall accuracy: xLAM2-32B 78.8, GPT-4o 68.0, Qwen3-8B 38.6. Fit Acc ~ exp(-(k*CL_total + b)): k = 0.034 (xLAM2), 0.067 (GPT-4o), 0.073 (Claude 3.7), 0.088 (Gemini 2.5 Pro), 0.075 (Qwen3-32B), 0.085 (Qwen3-8B).
limits: Authors set extraneous weight E by equating accuracy drops, so the total score is model-specific. Hosmer-Lemeshow p-values 0.10-0.89 for 9 models (no rejection of fit). Single benchmark, limited domain coverage.
agent_relevance: Gives a recipe: measure k (load sensitivity) per model and route or split tasks above its cliff.

source: Wang et al. (2026, AAAI) Beyond Accuracy: Cognitive Load Framework for Tool-use Agents (ToolLoad-Bench)
finding: Says prior LLM work used CLT as metaphor only, and lists neighbours: Sirbu et al. 2025 (explanation provision in LLM data assistants and extraneous load), Guidroz et al. 2025 (LLM text simplification and comprehension), Xiao and Yang 2025 (load-aware streaming).
numbers: Reference list only; those papers not opened individually.
limits: Third-party characterisation.
agent_relevance: Leads to follow up for human-facing germane or extraneous load studies with LLM output.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference (CLAI): Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Token Economy
finding: The only paper found that defines germane load for an LLM as productive tokens and builds a 3-stage meta-prompt: assess intrinsic load and decompose, cut extraneous context, then spend a token budget on structured stepwise reasoning with self-check (germane stage).
numbers: Llama-3-70B CoT vs CLAI-Prompt: GSM8K 92.5 vs 92.3 at 485 vs 310 tokens (-36.1%); MATH 53.9 vs 53.5 at 812 vs 525 (-35.3%). Llama-3-8B LongBench QA F1: full context 65.2 (4096 tokens), LLMLingua 68.1, RECOMP 67.5, CLAI-Prompt 69.3 (980 tokens, 4.2x).
limits: Single author, industry affiliation, no seeds or confidence intervals reported in the pages read, tidy numbers; treat as unreplicated. CLAI-Tune results (GSM8K 91.5 vs 90.1; HumanEval 74.8 vs 73.2; about -43% tokens) rest on the same single reports.
agent_relevance: Closest existing design to our schema idea of budget by difficulty, then reason in structured steps. Reproduce before trusting.

source: Zhang (2025) Cognitive Load-Aware Inference (CLAI): Neuro-Symbolic Framework for Token Economy
finding: GCL_LLM is defined as the share of generated tokens that carry productive reasoning, identified by high attention weight; ECL as low-attention tokens in context. A budget is set from the intrinsic-load estimate (example: 50 tokens for easy, 500 for hard).
numbers: Budget examples given in the paper text; no human-validated test that attention weight equals germane processing.
limits: Attention score as an importance measure is itself contested.
agent_relevance: Germane load for a model has no agreed meaning; any version we adopt must be defined by outcome (does it improve later solves), not by a proxy.

source: He et al. (2025, COLM) AdaptMI: Adaptive Skill-based In-context Math Instruction for Small Language Models
finding: Skill-based in-context examples (schema-like guidance) hurt small models on easy questions, a cognitive-overload and expertise-reversal analogue. Giving them only on hard questions fixes it.
numbers: Across 5 SLMs on MATH, average 4% drop on easy questions with skill-based examples vs non-skill-based; Table 2 shows drops of -10.3 and -8.7 points in some categories for Qwen2.5-1.5B. AdaptMI gains up to 3.6%, AdaptMI+ up to 6% Pass@1.
limits: Easy vs hard defined by a reward model per model; reasoning models and non-math domains untested here; improvements concentrated in the smallest models.
agent_relevance: Strong direct support for gating scaffolds by item difficulty. Do not apply the full schema to easy items.

source: He et al. (2025, COLM) AdaptMI: Adaptive Skill-based In-context Math Instruction for Small Language Models
finding: AdaptMI+ names the specific skills missing from the model's wrong answers and builds examples for those, then iterates; accuracy keeps rising over rounds for 1.5B-3B models.
numbers: Iterative loop up to 10 iterations on Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B/7B; iterative skill-based beats iterative random retrieval (Figure 2; values read from plot only).
limits: Gains saturate; 7B model gains are small.
agent_relevance: Mirrors schema acquisition from error: target the missing skill, not the whole method. Fits an error-driven repair operator.

source: Upadhayay et al. (2024) Cognitive Overload Attack: Prompt Injection for Long Context
finding: Applies intrinsic, extraneous and germane load definitions to in-context learning and shows that stacking tasks and distractors degrades model output until safety fails.
numbers: Attack success rate, Forbidden Question set: Claude-3-Opus 99.99%, GPT-4 90.95%, GPT-4-Turbo 89.22%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 84.05%, Gemini-1.0-Pro 75.43%. JailbreakBench: Claude-3-Opus 97%, Gemini-1.5-Pro 93%, Llama-3-70B 92%, GPT-4 90%, Gemini-1.0-Pro 49%.
limits: Offensive-security paper; load level is built by the attacker with six stages (CL0-CL5) and judged by LLM judges; overload is inferred from output failure, not measured. Gemini models failed to produce code from the INT stage onward.
agent_relevance: Evidence that overloaded context lowers both quality and guardrail adherence. Keep guardrails outside long working context and re-assert them each state.

source: Upadhayay et al. (2024) Cognitive Overload Attack: Prompt Injection for Long Context
finding: Quality of answers to a fixed question falls as extra tasks are stacked into the same prompt (Vicuna MT-Bench, 100 questions, pairwise vs CL0, three judge LLMs).
numbers: Pairwise judge scores averaged over Llama-3-70B, Gemini-1.5-Pro and GPT-4 judges across CL levels (Figure 7; values on plot only).
limits: Judge noise; no human check noted.
agent_relevance: One task per context window is the safe default; do not multitask a single call.

source: Upadhayay et al. (2024) Cognitive Overload Attack: Prompt Injection for Long Context
finding: The paper defines germane load for ICL as effort tying examples to prior knowledge; the authors argue models do not update weights so ICL learning is defined as correctly executing the task given the prompt.
numbers: Definition in Section 2, using Min et al. [35].
limits: Conceptual only; germane load is not manipulated experimentally in the paper.
agent_relevance: For fixed-weight models, schema building means the schema held in context, not stored learning.

source: Gong, Wan and Wang (2023/2024) Working Memory Capacity of ChatGPT: An Empirical Study
finding: ChatGPT shows an n-back capacity limit like humans: accuracy collapses around n=3 in verbal tasks; noise symbols cut it further; chain-of-thought raises scores but the limit persists.
numbers: Verbal n-back: d' drops to about 1 at n=3 for all but the noise variant, where capacity is lower. Spatial variants replicate with lower capacity; abstract spatial reasoning variants lower again. Typical human limit cited as n=3.
limits: ChatGPT-era models; text n-back is a task artefact; no germane load measure.
agent_relevance: Working memory limit is about interference and updating, so external notes help; supports compress-and-checkpoint states.

source: Gong and Zhang (2024) Self-Attention Limits Working Memory Capacity of Transformer-Based Models
finding: Small decoder-only transformers trained on n-back show attention score entropy rising with n, taken as the mechanism for the capacity limit.
numbers: Total attention-matrix entropy increases as N increases; attention concentrates at the N-back position during training.
limits: Toy trained models, not frontier LLMs; correlational link between entropy and error.
agent_relevance: Gives a mechanism reason for chunking and for keeping the number of simultaneously interacting items small.

source: Shang et al. (2026, TMLR) United Minds or Isolated Agents? CoThinker under Cognitive Load Theory
finding: Cross-check: CoThinker and CogniLoad both use proxies (attention entropy, distractor ratio, length) for load. Neither measures a human-style germane load.
numbers: See c01 and c05.
limits: Two independent teams chose different proxies, so there is no shared operationalisation.
agent_relevance: For our schema, log context size, interacting items per step and distractor share, and test which predicts errors.

source: Taneja, Singh and Goel (2026) Impact of Multimodal and Conversational AI on Learning Outcomes and Experience
finding: Randomized study of AI tutors with a CLT reading: conversational text-only AI felt easier and more engaging but gave the lowest post-test; interleaved text-and-image AI gave the highest. Authors read this as less extraneous load from conversation and more germane load from visual-verbal integration.
numbers: N=124 (162 completed, 17 excluded); ANOVA on post-test F(2,121)=4.60, p=.012, eta-squared=.071; MuDoC beat TexDoC p=.010, diff 0.69 (10-item MCQ); MuDoC vs DocSearch diff 0.47, p=.11 (not significant after Tukey). Pre-test did not differ between groups.
limits: Authors state cognitive load was not measured, so the germane-load story is interpretive. Single biology domain, Prolific adults, 94% aged 18-35.
agent_relevance: Easy-feeling AI help can reduce learning; for human-facing output, add effortful integration steps, not only fluency.

source: Taneja, Singh and Goel (2026) Impact of Multimodal and Conversational AI on Learning Outcomes and Experience
finding: Perception-performance gap: TexDoC was rated significantly easier to navigate and more engaging than DocSearch yet scored lowest.
numbers: Ease of navigation p=.002, eta-squared=.09; engagement p<.001, eta-squared=.12 (conversational vs DocSearch).
limits: Ratings are self-report.
agent_relevance: Fluency is a poor proxy for learning; do not use user ease ratings as the reward for the agent.

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing
finding: EEG study: connectivity scaled down with external support (Brain-only strongest, Search intermediate, LLM weakest); LLM group could not quote their own essays and reported low ownership.
numbers: 54 participants in sessions 1-3 (18 per group), only 18 completed session 4 (LLM-to-Brain and Brain-to-LLM swap). Four sessions over four months.
limits: Preprint, under review; small N, high dropout in session 4; EEG connectivity read by authors as lower engagement; no germane-load measure; essay task only.
agent_relevance: Offloading may remove the effortful schema-building part. Test whether our agent's notes are actually re-used or only stored.

source: Bastani et al. (2025, PNAS) Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning
finding: Field experiment with about 1,000 high-school maths students: unrestricted GPT-4 access raised practice scores but lowered later no-AI exam scores; a tutor version with hints and teacher-written guardrails removed the harm.
numbers: From memory, not opened (PNAS returned 403): practice +48% (GPT Base) and +127% (GPT Tutor); exam about -17% for GPT Base, no significant loss for GPT Tutor. Verify before citing.
limits: Numbers recalled, not read this session.
agent_relevance: Guardrailed scaffolding that keeps the learner doing the work is the germane-load-preserving design; direct answers are not.

source: Liao et al. (2026, WWW) Prism: Lowering User Cognitive Load in LLMs via Complex Intent Understanding
finding: CLT-inspired clarification: decomposes a complex user intent into elements and orders clarification questions by logical dependency, aiming to cut the user's intrinsic and extraneous load.
numbers: Reported: logical conflicts in clarification questions 11.5%; user satisfaction +14.4%; task completion time -34.8%; EEG power-spectral cognitive-load comparison in a user study.
limits: Load here is the human user's, not the model's; small EEG sample not examined in detail; germane load not addressed.
agent_relevance: Ask few, dependency-ordered clarifying questions; matches a clarify state.

source: Search note: arXiv listing for 'cognitive load theory' + 'language models'
finding: Gap found: no paper in this search directly manipulates a germane-load-like factor (self-explanation prompts, schema prompts) on LLMs with a CLT control. Germane load appears only as a length proxy (CogniLoad) or an attention-token definition (CLAI).
numbers: The arXiv listing returned 16 results (Jun 2024 to Oct 2026), none a direct germane-load manipulation.
limits: One query plus follow-ups, not the full literature; WebSearch budget was exhausted so non-arXiv venues were not searched.
agent_relevance: Germane load for LLM agents is an open question; any claim in our schema should be flagged untested.
